title: GL read-back single-transaction FOUR-leg accrual (loan 12 L30: interest pair plus penalty pair) posts one receivable/income pair per charge family
_note: Parity vector transcribing the loan-produced journal-entry batch read back from the journal-entries endpoint for loan entityId 12, transactionId L30, the SECOND accrual in the committed capture that carries TWO CHARGE FAMILIES. LN-L25 (same capture, same shape) carries the interest and FEE families; L30 carries the interest and PENALTY families, so together the two vectors cover all THREE charge families this capture observes (interest, fees, penalties) and show that the property is per-FAMILY, not fee-specific. The batch is four legs in ONE transaction id forming TWO BALANCED PAIRS, each family using its OWN account pair: DEBIT OHLGR-Interest-Receivable 841.51 / CREDIT OHLGR-Interest-On-Loans 841.51 (interest family) and DEBIT OHLGR-Penalties-Receivable 57.00 / CREDIT OHLGR-Income-From-Penalties 57.00 (penalty family). request.journal_entries transcribes each leg's transactionId, glAccountName, entryType.value and amount; amounts are raised to integer minor units (841.51 -> 84151, 57.00 -> 5700) with no residue. expect.journal_entry_debits_minor and expect.journal_entry_credits_minor are the two independent side totals (89851 each), each transcribed as the sum over EVERY leg, never a netting. expect.journal_entry_account_sides is the third expected cell: WHICH account takes WHICH side in WHICH transaction. The defect this vector exists to catch is the same as LN-L25's and is NOT specific to the fee family: a port that routes ALL accrual income to a single income account keeps every leg, every side and both totals at the observed values and moves only WHICH income account the penalty family's credit names; the per-(transaction, account) side list is the only cell that goes red. The accrual satisfies the seam's existing multiLegDistinctCredits admission predicate unchanged: ONE transaction id, FOUR legs (>=3) and TWO distinct credit accounts; admission was NOT widened for it. Nothing was computed by this promotion; every cell is a transcription of the oracle's generated postings.

provenance.note: request.journal_entries and both expected totals are transcribed from the four pageItems of the committed capture journalentries-loan-12-after-raw.json whose entityType.value is LOAN, entityId is 12 and transactionId is L30 (entry ids 43, 46, 50, 52). capture_case_id names the transaction the batch comprises, exactly as LN-L12 names L53 in the same capture. The capture is a filtered journal-entries page (totalFilteredRecords 29), so it is identified by the transaction id rather than an externalId. expect.journal_entry_account_sides is transcribed from the same four pageItems, keying each (transactionId, glAccountName) to its entryType.value; no side is inferred from an account's normal balance. Both families are observed, not derived: the interest pair is ids 43/46 and the penalty pair is ids 50/52.
